**Describe the bug** `compute_final_q_score` in `OmniGibson/omnigibson/eval/utils/score_utils.py` accepts result files for 20 public instances per task and divides every per-task sum by 20. The 2026 challenge docs say a full submission is 10 instances per task and that the other 10 public instances are not used for reporting. Code at `b544acb`: - `eval_utils.py:19`: `NUM_PUBLIC_TEST_INSTANCES = 20` (and `NUM_HIDDEN_TEST_INSTANCES = 20` on line 20). - `score_utils.py:291-299`: `possible_filenames` is built from `TEST_INSTANCE_IDS[:NUM_PUBLIC_TEST_INSTANCES]`, so files for all 20 public instances pass the name check on line 313. - `score_utils.py:300`: `n_instances_per_task = NUM_PUBLIC_TEST_INSTANCES if testset == "public" else NUM_HIDDEN_TEST_INSTANCES`. - `score_utils.py:340-341`: `q_score_avg[task_name] = sum(...) / n_instances_per_task`, and the same divisor for `task_sr` and the time and distance scores. Docs at the same commit: - `docs/challenge/evaluation.md`: "Use the first 10 public instances, corresponding to instance indices 0-9 ... for evaluation results" and "The remaining 10 public instances, indices 10-19, are not used for leaderboard reporting". - `docs/challenge/submission.md`: "Full evaluation size: 100 tasks x 10 instances x 1 rollout = 1,000 rollout outputs." - `docs/challenge/evaluation.md`, hidden set: "We will hold out 10 more instances for final evaluation." Two consequences if this function (or the constants) is what scores a submission: 1. A complete submission that follows the docs and succeeds on every rollout gets `q_score` 0.5, not 1.0. Every compliant score is halved. 2. A submission that also includes instances 10-19 passes the file-name check and is scored on 20 rollouts per task, so its attainable score is twice that of a compliant submission from the same policy. If both kinds were ranked together, they are not comparable. For an honest team the direction is down, so this is mostly an under-report. I do not know what the 2026 leaderboard backend runs, so I cannot say whether any published number is affected. **To Reproduce** No simulator is needed, this is the aggregation function only. The attached script loads the real `score_utils.py` and `eval_utils.py`, builds result JSONs in the shape `record_fn` writes for a two-task `B100_task_misc.csv`, and calls `compute_final_q_score` on four submission directories. Output: ``` NUM_PUBLIC_TEST_INSTANCES = 20 | documented reporting instances: indices 0-9 -> 301 .. 310 follows docs (10 instances), succeeds on every rollout files= 20 q_score=0.500 task_sr=0.500 also submits indices 10-19, succeeds on every rollout files= 40 q_score=1.000 task_sr=1.000 follows docs (10 instances), 50% success files= 20 q_score=0.250 task_sr=0.250 also submits indices 10-19, same 50% success policy files= 40 q_score=0.500 task_sr=0.500 ``` (`files=20` is 2 tasks x 10 instances.) **Expected behavior** The divisor and the accepted file set match the documented protocol: 10 instances per task for the public set (ids 301-310), and whatever the hidden-set size really is. For example a `NUM_REPORTED_PUBLIC_INSTANCES = 10` used for both `possible_filenames` and `n_instances_per_task`, with files for ids 311-320 rejected or ignored. If 20 is the intended number, then the docs are what needs changing. **Screenshots** None. **Desktop (please complete the following information):** - OS: macOS (the function under test is pure Python) - Isaac Sim Version: not used - OmniGibson Version: repository at commit `b544acb` **Additional context** "Missing rollout instances count as zero" is documented in `submission.md`, and I am not questioning that rule. The point is the size it is measured against: the docs say 10 per task, the code uses 20. There is no test for `score_utils` in `OmniGibson/tests`. Happy to send a PR once you say which number is intended. The files referred to above are in the collapsed blocks below.
score_utils_denominator_20_vs_documented_10.py ```python """BEHAVIOR-1K: score_utils divides by 20 instances per task; the documented protocol is 10. Real code under test (pristine clone at /path/to/BEHAVIOR-1K, loaded by path, not modified): OmniGibson/omnigibson/eval/utils/score_utils.py sanity_check_filename, compute_final_q_score OmniGibson/omnigibson/eval/utils/eval_utils.py NUM_PUBLIC_TEST_INSTANCES = 20 (line 19), TEST_INSTANCE_IDS = 301..340 (line 21) Documented protocol (docs/challenge/evaluation.md, docs/challenge/submission.md): "Use the first 10 public instances, corresponding to instance indices 0-9 ... for evaluation results", "The remaining 10 public instances, indices 10-19, are not used for leaderboard reporting", "Full evaluation size: 100 tasks x 10 instances x 1 rollout = 1,000 rollout outputs". score_utils.compute_final_q_score: line 291-299 accepts result files for all 20 public instance ids (301..320) line 300 n_instances_per_task = NUM_PUBLIC_TEST_INSTANCES (20) line 340-341 q_score_avg = sum(q) / 20 ; task_sr = count(q == 1) / 20 So a complete submission that follows the documented protocol and succeeds on every rollout is scored 0.5, and a submission that also includes the ten instances the docs exclude is scored on twice as many rollouts. Stand-ins: `omnigibson.macros.gm` is replaced by an object whose DATA_PATH points at a temp dir holding a two-task B100_task_misc.csv (the real file ships with the dataset, not the repo). The result JSONs are constructed in the shape evaluator.py record_fn writes. Run with python (eval_utils imports torch). Prints B1K-SCORE-DENOMINATOR-DISAGREES-WITH-DOCUMENTED-PROTOCOL only when it fires. """ import contextlib import importlib.util import io import json import os import sys import tempfile import types from pathlib import Path CLONE = Path(__import__("os").environ.get("RT_CLONE", "/path/to/BEHAVIOR-1K/OmniGibson")) TASKS = ["turning_on_radio", "picking_up_trash"] def load(name, rel): spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, CLONE / rel) m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) sys.modules[name] = m spec.loader.exec_module(m) return m def write_submission(root: Path, name: str, instance_ids, q_of): d = root / name / "json" d.mkdir(parents=True) for task in TASKS: for iid in instance_ids: q = q_of(task, iid) result = { "task": task, "instance_id": iid, "rollout_id": 0, "steps": 1000, "success": q == 1.0, "agent_distance": {"base": 2.0, "left": 1.5, "right": 1.2}, "normalized_agent_distance": {"base": 1.0, "left": 1.0, "right": 1.0}, "q_score": {"final": q}, "time": {"simulator_steps": 1000, "simulator_time": 33.3, "normalized_time": 1.0}, } (d / f"{task}_{iid}_0.json").write_text(json.dumps(result)) return root / name def main() -> int: tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="b1k_score_")) meta = tmp / "data" / "2026-challenge-task-instances" / "metadata" meta.mkdir(parents=True) with open(meta / "B100_task_misc.csv", "w", newline="") as f: f.write("Task,Task ID,Rooms to inlcude\n") for i, t in enumerate(TASKS): f.write(f"{t},{i},living_room_0\n") for pkg in ("omnigibson", "omnigibson.eval", "omnigibson.eval.utils"): sys.modules[pkg] = types.ModuleType(pkg) sys.modules[pkg].__path__ = [] macros = types.ModuleType("omnigibson.macros") macros.gm = types.SimpleNamespace(DATA_PATH=str(tmp / "data")) sys.modules["omnigibson.macros"] = macros eval_utils = load("omnigibson.eval.utils.eval_utils", "omnigibson/eval/utils/eval_utils.py") score_utils = load("omnigibson.eval.utils.score_utils", "omnigibson/eval/utils/score_utils.py") ids = eval_utils.TEST_INSTANCE_IDS first10, first20 = ids[:10], ids[:20] print("NUM_PUBLIC_TEST_INSTANCES =", eval_utils.NUM_PUBLIC_TEST_INSTANCES, "| documented reporting instances: indices 0-9 ->", first10[0], "..", first10[-1]) subs = tmp / "subs" out = tmp / "out" out.mkdir() perfect = lambda task, iid: 1.0 # noqa: E731 half = lambda task, iid: 1.0 if iid % 2 else 0.0 # noqa: E731 cases = [ ("standard.public.Compliant_perfect.Lab.20261111", first10, perfect, "follows docs (10 instances), succeeds on every rollout"), ("standard.public.Twenty_perfect.Lab.20261111", first20, perfect, "also submits indices 10-19, succeeds on every rollout"), ("standard.public.Compliant_half.Lab.20261111", first10, half, "follows docs (10 instances), 50% success"), ("standard.public.Twenty_half.Lab.20261111", first20, half, "also submits indices 10-19, same 50% success policy"), ] scores = {} for name, inst, qf, desc in cases: path = write_submission(subs, name, inst, qf) with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()): score_utils.sanity_check_filename(str(path)) # real score_utils.compute_final_q_score(str(path), str(out)) # real res = json.load(open(out / f"{name}.json"))["overall_scores"] scores[name] = res print(f" {desc:58s} files={len(inst) * len(TASKS):3d} " f"q_score={res['q_score']:.3f} task_sr={res['task_sr']:.3f}") a = new_candidates.body:
### Ticket Type

Bug report

### Environment & System Info

Current main `e581c1d5701f846788662079d4ac08835c96def9`, Linux, Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.2.6, PyArrow 25.0.1, datasets 4.8.5. Local CPU reproduction, no robot or downloaded dataset required.

### Description

Recording a one-frame episode next to a longer episode can fail when their metadata is flushed in separate batches. Integer statistics such as `frame_index.min` are serialized as integers for one frame and doubles for multiple frames, so the later batch disagrees with the Parquet writer's schema.

This also occurs with the default buffer size: ten two-frame episodes followed by one single-frame episode fail during `finalize()`. Ten single-frame episodes followed by a two-frame episode fail in the opposite direction.

### Context & Reproduction

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import mkdtemp

import numpy as np
from lerobot.datasets import LeRobotDataset

dataset = LeRobotDataset.create(
    "local/singleton-schema",
    root=Path(mkdtemp()) / "dataset",
    fps=10,
    features={"state": {"dtype": "float32", "shape": (2,), "names": None}},
    use_videos=False,
    metadata_buffer_size=1,
)
for length in [2, 1]:
    for frame in range(length):
        dataset.add_frame({"state": np.full(2, frame, dtype=np.float32), "task": "test"})
    dataset.save_episode()
dataset.finalize()
```

`[1, 2]` also fails. `[2, 3]` and `[1, 1]` complete and reopen correctly. To exercise the default-sized buffer, set `metadata_buffer_size=10` and use `[2] * 10 + [1]` or `[1] * 10 + [2]`.

### Relevant logs

```text
dataset_metadata.py, _flush_metadata_buffer: self._pq_writer.write_table(table)
ValueError: Table schema does not match schema used to create file
stats/frame_index/min: list<item: int64>
vs. stats/frame_index/min: list<item: double>
```

`get_feature_stats()` routes one sample through `_compute_basic_stats`, which preserves integer extrema; its multi-sample accumulator promotes the input to float64. Metadata serialization then infers different Arrow types from those values. Expected behavior: supported episode lengths can be recorded together and reopened with their data and statistics intact.

### Checklist

- [x] Searched matching Issues and PRs, including related statistics work.
- [x] Reproduced on the current main commit above.
- [ ] Verified on a second environment.

AI assisted with investigation and writing.
new_candidates.title: fix(datasets): single-frame episodes cause metadata schema mismatches

new_candidates.body:
### Ticket Type

🐛 Bug Report (Something isn't working)

### Environment & System Info

```Shell
- LeRobot version: 0.7.1 (main @ e581c1d5)
- Platform: Linux-5.15.0-144-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35
- Python version: 3.12.16
- Transformers version: 5.22.2
- PyTorch version: 2.8.0+cu128
- Is PyTorch built with CUDA support?: Yes
- Using GPU in script?: Yes (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090)
```

### Description

Flow-matching VLA policies zero-pad the action chunk to `max_action_dim` (`pad_vector`, `src/lerobot/policies/common/vla_utils.py:116`) and then **slice the padded columns out of the loss**:

| policy | pad to `max_action_dim` | loss truncated to the real dof |
|---|---|---|
| pi0 | `modeling_pi0.py:1073` | `modeling_pi0.py:1151` |
| pi05 | `modeling_pi05.py:1488` | `modeling_pi05.py:1596` |
| smolvla | `modeling_smolvla.py:470` | `modeling_smolvla.py:325` |
| eo1 | `modeling_eo1.py:150` | `modeling_eo1.py:572` |

So the predicted velocity on those columns, `v_pad`, never receives any gradient.

At inference, however, the padded columns are still part of `x_t` and are still updated by **every** Euler step. `sample_actions` draws noise of shape `(B, chunk_size, max_action_dim)` (`modeling_smolvla.py:791`, `modeling_pi05.py:955-960`) and `euler_integrate` (`common/flow_matching.py:355-415`) does `x_t <- x_t + dt * v_t` over all of them. They are only sliced off at the very end (`modeling_smolvla.py:226`, `modeling_pi05.py:1549`) — after having been fed back through

```python
self.action_in_proj = nn.Linear(self.config.max_action_dim, expert_hidden_size)   # modeling_smolvla.py:564
```

at every step. That projection mixes all `max_action_dim` columns into every action token, so the drifting padded columns condition the velocity predicted for the **real** dims on the next step, and the deviation accumulates as the loop proceeds.

### The padded columns have a closed-form trajectory, and the model is not asked to follow it

Under `NOISE_AT_ONE` (`common/flow_matching.py:246-248`):

```python
x_t = t * noise + (1 - t) * actions
velocity_target = noise - actions
```

The padded clean action is exactly `0` (`pad_vector` pads with zeros), so the padded columns are analytically determined:

```
x_pad(t) = t * eps_pad          v_pad = eps_pad
```

i.e. their norm must decay linearly to zero as `t: 1 -> 0`. Nothing enforces this, because those columns are not in the loss.

### Observed behaviour

Instrumenting `denoise_step` and tracking the norm of the padded columns of `x_t`, relative to the norm of the padded columns of the starting noise (SmolVLA, real action dim 34 / `max_action_dim` 64, so 30 of 64 columns are padding; averaged over 3 noise draws):

```
num_steps=10    step      0      2      5      7      9    t=0
                ratio  1.000  1.007  1.038  1.070  1.108  1.129

num_steps=25    step      0      6     12     18     24    t=0
                ratio  1.000  1.009  1.035  1.074  1.120  1.128

num_steps=50    step      0     12     25     37     49    t=0
                ratio  1.000  1.009  1.038  1.077  1.124  1.127

num_steps=100   step      0     25     50     75     99    t=0
                ratio  1.000  1.010  1.038  1.079  1.125  1.127
```

The padded columns **inflate monotonically relative to the noise scale they started at**, and end the loop at ~1.13x that scale. Since the padded clean action is `0`, the flow's own interpolation requires them to arrive at `t = 0` with norm `0` — they arrive 13% *larger* than they began.

The sweep is the important part: 10, 25, 50 and 100 Euler steps all converge to the same 1.127-1.129. This is not a discretisation artefact that a finer integrator would fix — it is the exact solution of the velocity field the network actually learned on those columns, and that field is unconstrained precisely because those columns are missing from the loss.

Every one of those steps then reads the inflated, off-scale padded columns back in through `action_in_proj` when predicting the velocity for the real dims.

### For smolvla this is a regression from #3133

Before [#3133](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/3133) (merged 2026-03-11, superseding [#1260](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/1260)), smolvla's loss ended with

```python
losses = losses[:, :, : self.config.max_action_dim]   # a no-op: losses are already max_action_dim
```

so the padded columns **were** supervised. #3133 changed it to the real dof, motivated by "consistency with the unpadding operation in `select_action`". That reasoning holds for the *output*, but misses that the padded columns are also an *input* to the next denoise step.

Consequence: `smolvla_base` was trained with these columns supervised, and every LeRobot fine-tune since removes that supervision. pi0 / pi05 never had it (the truncation has been there since #1910).

This is orthogonal to #5105 / #5106 / #5108, which concern **temporal** end-of-episode padding (`action_is_pad`). This is about **feature-dim** padding to `max_action_dim`.


### Context & Reproduction

Wrap `denoise_step` and log the norm of the padded columns of `x_t`, normalised by the norm of the padded columns of the starting noise:

```python
real_dim = policy.config.action_feature.shape[0]
model = policy.model
orig = model.denoise_step

torch.manual_seed(0)
noise = model.sample_noise((1, policy.config.chunk_size, policy.config.max_action_dim), "cuda")
eps_pad_norm = noise[..., real_dim:].norm().item()

def traced(prefix_pad_masks, past_key_values, x_t, timestep):
    ratio = x_t[..., real_dim:].norm().item() / eps_pad_norm
    print(f"t={float(timestep.flatten()[0]):.3f}  ||x_pad|| / ||eps_pad|| = {ratio:.3f}")
    return orig(prefix_pad_masks, past_key_values, x_t, timestep)

model.denoise_step = traced
policy.predict_action_chunk(batch, noise=noise)
```

The ratio starts at 1.000 and should fall to 0. On `main` it rises monotonically to ~1.13. Raising `policy.config.num_steps` to 25 / 50 / 100 does not change the endpoint.

### Relevant logs or stack trace

```Shell

```

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing tickets to ensure this isn't a duplicate.
- [x] I am using the latest version of the `main` branch.
- [x] I have verified this is not an environment-specific problem.

### Additional Info / Workarounds

- Related: #2559 (jitter vs. openpi — the same mechanism was independently identified in the comments), #3133 / #1260 (the change that removed the supervision for smolvla), openpi PR [Physical-Intelligence/openpi#871](https://github.com/Physical-Intelligence/openpi/pull/871) (proposes the *opposite* change in openpi, citing LeRobot's mask as the motivation — the two repos should be reconciled explicitly).
- Workaround until fixed: when training from scratch, set `max_action_dim` equal to the real action dim so there are no padded columns. Not available when fine-tuning a published base checkpoint.
- Unrelated, hit while reproducing: `policies/praxis/praxis_core/layers.py:59` and `action_expert.py:60` need torch >= 2.9 (`test_configs.force_filter_reduction_configs`, `flex_attention.FlexKernelOptions`), but `pyproject.toml` declares `torch>=2.7`, so importing `lerobot.policies` fails on torch 2.8. Probably worth a separate ticket.
new_candidates.title: pi0 / pi05 / smolvla / eo1: padded action dims are dropped from the flow-matching loss but still integrated at inference, so they drift off the training manifold and leak into the real dims

### Describe the bug

`OccupancyMap.check_world_point_in_bounds()` and `check_world_point_in_freespace()` in `isaaclab_mimic.locomanipulation_sdg.occupancy_map_utils` convert the fractional pixel coordinate with `int()`, which truncates toward zero. A world point up to one pixel past the left edge (`-x`) or the top edge (`+y`) of the map maps to a pixel coordinate in `(-1, 0)`, `int()` turns that into `0`, and the point is reported as inside the map. `check_world_point_in_freespace()` then reads the freespace value of the edge pixel for a point that is not on the map at all.

The right and bottom edges are not affected, so the check is asymmetric. `plan_path()` in `path_utils.py` uses the same `int()` before its `check_pixel_in_bounds()` guard, so a start or goal just past the left or top edge is not rejected and is handed to the path planner. `clear_nav_map_buffer()` in `scripts/imitation_learning/locomanipulation_sdg/generate_data.py` does the same with `astype(int)`.

### Steps to reproduce

CPU only, no simulator needed:

```python
import numpy as np
from isaaclab_mimic.locomanipulation_sdg.occupancy_map_utils import OccupancyMap, Point2d

occ = np.zeros((10, 10), dtype=bool)
omap = OccupancyMap.from_masks(~occ, occ, 0.1, (0.0, 0.0, 0.0))  # covers [0, 1) m in x and y

for x, y in [(-0.05, 0.5), (0.5, 1.05), (1.05, 0.5), (0.5, -0.05)]:
    p = Point2d(x=x, y=y)
    print((x, y), omap.check_world_point_in_bounds(p), omap.check_world_point_in_freespace(p))
```

Output on `main`:

```
(-0.05, 0.5) True True
(0.5, 1.05) True True
(1.05, 0.5) False False
(0.5, -0.05) False False
```

All four points are 0.05 m outside the map; only the right and bottom ones are rejected.

### Expected behavior

All four points are out of bounds and not in freespace. Flooring the pixel coordinate (`math.floor` / `np.floor`) instead of truncating gives that, and leaves every point inside the map unchanged.

### System Info

- Commit: e670e2c2b9e0bc9ccc92ed95104ccb9cc3229f75 (`main`)
- Isaac Sim Version: not needed (pure python, reproduced on CPU)
- OS: Linux
- Python: 3.13, numpy, opencv-python-headless, usd-core

### Additional context

I have a small fix with a regression test ready and will open a PR.

### Checklist

- [x] I have checked that there is no similar issue in the repo (**required**)
- [x] I have checked that the issue is not in running Isaac Sim itself and is related to the repo

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] World points just past any edge of the occupancy map are reported out of bounds and not in freespace
- [ ] `plan_path()` rejects a start or goal just past the left or top edge

ManiSkill has a code path for a newer SAPIEN render system, added in #480 (commit e08e3dc):

- detection: mani_skill/render/version.py checks from sapien.wrapper.scene import get_camera_shader_pack
- update: scene.py#L439 (https://github.com/mani-skill/ManiSkill/blob/62ff3a5896b4d5b4cf0ac4c8d79afe600c9404a3/mani_skill/envs/scene.py#L439) (_sapien_31_update_render, sapien.render.GpuSyncManager.sync())
- setup: _sapien_31_setup_gpu_rendering (L1092) and _sapien_31_gpu_setup_sensors (L1173, sapien.render.RenderManager(get_shader_pack(...)))

I couldn't find these APIs in any public SAPIEN version. I checked tags up to 3.0.3, the nightly tag (7dba23f, branch upgrade/physx5.11-cp311-315), master (788fd0a) and dev (6a50b78). None of them have sapien.wrapper.scene.get_camera_shader_pack, GpuSyncManager or RenderManager.

Use case: we evaluate VLA policies on RoboTwin-style scenes (dual-arm Aloha, 4 cameras at 320x240). Observations must be ray traced (rt, 32 spp, path depth 8, OptiX denoiser). We want to run physx_cuda with many sub-scenes (num_envs 64–256) and render RT observations for every sub-scene at action-chunk boundaries.

In SAPIEN 3.0.x the GPU-batched rendering path only supports rasterization:

- SapienRenderCameraComponent::getCudaBuffer throws "only rasterization renderer supports camera cuda buffer." (camera_component.cpp)
- BatchedRenderSystem::update writes poses into the rasterizer's transform buffer, but the RT renderer rebuilds its TLAS from CPU-side transforms (svulkan2 Scene::updateTLAS), so GPU-written poses never reach ray tracing.
- ManiSkill also asserts that ray-tracing shaders don't work with parallel rendering (scene.py#L1221).
- 

Questions:

1. Where can we get the SAPIEN build that provides the "3.1" render system (GpuSyncManager, RenderManager, get_camera_shader_pack)? Is it planned for a public release, and roughly when?
2. In that render system, does RenderManager support the rt shader pack with GPU simulation across sub-scenes? That is, are TLAS instance transforms and camera poses updated on the GPU?
3. If not, is px.sync_poses_gpu_to_cpu() followed by per-sub-scene update_render() and take_picture() the recommended way to get RT images with physx_cuda today?


Environment: Linux, NVIDIA Blackwell (sm_120) GPUs, CUDA 12.8, SAPIEN 3.0.0b1, ManiSkill at 62ff3a5.

**What happens** `get_epoch` in `calvin_models/calvin_agent/evaluation/evaluate_policy.py` (lines 42-45) computes the epoch and drops it: ```python def get_epoch(checkpoint): if "=" not in checkpoint.stem: return "0" checkpoint.stem.split("=")[1] ``` For any checkpoint named `epoch=N.ckpt` it returns `None`. That value is passed to `evaluate_policy(..., epoch, ...)` (line 252) and on to `print_and_save` (line 119), which uses it as the key of the entry it merges into `results.json` (`evaluation/utils.py:115-126`) and then prints (`:127-130`): ```python print( f"Best model: epoch {max(json_data, key=lambda x: json_data[x]['avg_seq_len'])} " f"with average sequences length of {max(map(lambda x: x['avg_seq_len'], json_data.values()))}" ) ``` Effects: 1. Every checkpoint is stored under the key `null`. With `--checkpoints` or `--last_k_checkpoints`, `results.json` cannot say which checkpoint scored what. 2. The file ends up with two `null` keys (the one read back from disk is the string `"null"`, the new one is `None`, and both are written). On the next read only the last one survives. 3. The default log directory is shared (`/evaluation`, else `/tmp/evaluation`, `utils.py:146-156`). The closing "Best model" line takes the maximum over whatever is in that file, so after evaluating a weak model it can print the average sequence length of the model evaluated before it, labelled `epoch null`. The numbers that matter are not affected: the "Average successful sequence length" line, the 1/5 to 5/5 chain success rates and the per-task table are computed from the current run only and are correct. What is wrong is the epoch label, the persisted file, and the last printed line for anyone who reads only that line. **Reproduction** The attached script calls the real `get_epoch`, `count_success` and `print_and_save` (torch, hydra, pytorch_lightning and calvin_env are replaced by import-only stand-ins; none is called). Model A scores chains of 4, then model B scores chains of 1 into the same log directory. Output at `fa03f01`: ``` get_epoch for epoch=10/20/30.ckpt: [None, None, None] model A: Average successful sequence length: 4.0 model B: Average successful sequence length: 1.0 model B closing line: Best model: epoch null with average sequences length of 4.0 results.json top-level keys: ['null', 'null'] ``` **Fix** One line: ```diff def get_epoch(checkpoint): if "=" not in checkpoint.stem: return "0" - checkpoint.stem.split("=")[1] + return checkpoint.stem.split("=")[1] ``` With that change the same script prints: ``` get_epoch for epoch=10/20/30.ckpt: ['10', '20', '30'] model A: Average successful sequence length: 4.0 model B: Average successful sequence length: 1.0 model B closing line: Best model: epoch 99 with average sequences length of 4.0 results.json top-level keys: ['99', '10'] ``` The keys are right and the file is valid. The "Best model" line still reports model A's entry, because the default log directory is shared between runs; it is now labelled with A's epoch, so a reader can at least see it is not the checkpoint just evaluated. If you want that line to cover only the current invocation, it needs a per-run log directory by default or a filter on the checkpoints evaluated in this call. I left that alone because it changes behaviour people may rely on. I can open the one-line change as a PR. The files referred to above are in the collapsed blocks below.
results_json_epoch_none_best_model.py ```python """CALVIN: calvin_agent/evaluation/evaluate_policy.py get_epoch() has no `return` on its main branch, so every checkpoint named `epoch=N.ckpt` is logged under the key None. print_and_save() merges into /results.json (default log dir is shared: /evaluation or /tmp/evaluation) and then prints "Best model: epoch ... with average sequences length of max(...)" over everything in that file. Effects shown with the real functions: 1. epochs 10, 20, 30 of one training run all map to None; 2. results.json ends up with duplicate "null" keys (invalid as a record of which checkpoint scored what); 3. the closing "Best model" line of a weak model's evaluation prints the average sequence length of an earlier, different model left in the same directory. Real code: get_epoch() from evaluate_policy.py; count_success() and print_and_save() from evaluation/utils.py. Stand-ins: torch, hydra, omegaconf, pytorch_lightning, termcolor, pyhash, calvin_env (import only; none are called). Run: python results_json_epoch_none_best_model.py """ import contextlib import io import json import os import sys import tempfile from pathlib import Path sys.dont_write_bytecode = True sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))) import sim_stubs # noqa: E402 CLONE = os.environ.get("CALVIN_CLONE", "/path/to/calvin") sim_stubs.install(["torch", "hydra", "omegaconf", "pytorch_lightning", "termcolor", "pyhash", "calvin_env", "git", "sentence_transformers", "torchvision", "MulticoreTSNE", "plotly", "wandb", "matplotlib"]) sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(CLONE, "calvin_models")) from calvin_agent.evaluation import evaluate_policy as EP # noqa: E402 from calvin_agent.evaluation import utils as U # noqa: E402 epochs = [EP.get_epoch(Path(f"/runs/model_b/saved_models/epoch={n}.ckpt")) for n in (10, 20, 30)] print("get_epoch for epoch=10/20/30.ckpt:", epochs) seq = ({}, ("open_drawer", "turn_on_led", "move_slider_left", "lift_red_block_table", "place_in_drawer")) log_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="calvin_a8_")) def evaluate(results, epoch): out = io.StringIO() with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out): U.print_and_save(results, [seq] * len(results), log_dir, epoch) # the real writer lines = out.getvalue().strip().splitlines() return lines[1], lines[-1] # Monday: a strong model A is evaluated, chains of 4 on average. a_avg, a_best = evaluate([4] * 10, EP.get_epoch(Path("/runs/model_a/epoch=99.ckpt"))) # Tuesday: a weak model B is evaluated into the same (default) log dir. b_avg, b_best = evaluate([1] * 10, EP.get_epoch(Path("/runs/model_b/epoch=10.ckpt"))) print("model A:", a_avg) print("model B:", b_avg) print("model B closing line:", b_best) raw = open(log_dir / "results.json").read() print("results.json top-level keys:", [k for k, _ in json.loads(raw, object_pairs_hook=list)]) if epochs == [None, None, None] and "4.0" in b_best and "1.0" in b_avg: print("CALVIN-BEST-MODEL-LINE-REPORTS-ANOTHER-RUN-AND-EPOCH-KEY-IS-NONE") else: print("calvin results.json defect not reproduced") ```
sim_stubs.py ```python """Shared stand-in importer for these reproductions. install(roots) registers a meta path finder so that `import .` yields an empty stand-in module whose attributes are permissive dummy classes. Used only for heavy third-party imports (carla, py_trees, nuplan, hydra, torch, robosuite, ...). The repo code under test is always the real file from the pristine clone. """ import importlib.abc import importlib.machinery import sys import types sys.dont_write_bytecode = True # never write __pycache__ into a pristine clone class _DummyMeta(type): def __getattr__(cls, name): # attribute of a stand-in class is another stand-in class, so that # `class X(py_trees.behaviour.Behaviour)` still defines a real class X if name.startswith("__"): raise AttributeError(name) sub = _DummyMeta(name, (Dummy,), {}) setattr(cls, name, sub) return sub def __iter__(cls): return iter(()) class Dummy(metaclass=_DummyMeta): def __init__(self, *a, **k): pass def __call__(self, *a, **k): return Dummy() def __getattr__(self, name): if name.startswith("__"): raise AttributeError(name) return Dummy() def __iter__(self): return iter(()) def __bool__(self): return False class _AutoMod(types.ModuleType): def __getattr__(self, name): if name.startswith("__"): raise AttributeError(name) obj = _DummyMeta(name, (Dummy,), {}) setattr(self, name, obj) return obj class _Finder(importlib.abc.MetaPathFinder, importlib.abc.Loader): def __init__(self, roots): self.roots = set(roots) def find_spec(self, fullname, path=None, target=None): if fullname.split(".")[0] in self.roots: return importlib.machinery.ModuleSpec(fullname, self, is_package=True) return None def create_module(self, spec): m = _AutoMod(spec.name) m.__path__ = [] return m def exec_module(self, module): pass def install(roots): sys.meta_path.insert(0, _Finder(roots)) ```
calvin-ISSUE1-get-epoch-missing-return-results-keyed-none.patch ```diff From 2bb845a13f2e24a3854f7a38ccbee2b12fb988af Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001 From: AUTHENSOR <250658088+AUTHENSOR@users.noreply.github.com> Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 20:12:17 -0800 Subject: [PATCH] Return the epoch from get_epoch in evaluate_policy get_epoch() computed checkpoint.stem.split("=")[1] and discarded it, so every checkpoint named epoch=N.ckpt was logged under the key None and results.json could not tell checkpoints apart. --- calvin_models/calvin_agent/evaluation/evaluate_policy.py | 2 +- 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-) diff --git a/calvin_models/calvin_agent/evaluation/evaluate_policy.py b/calvin_models/calvin_agent/evaluation/evaluate_policy.py index 1f30e47..db7ad86 100644 --- a/calvin_models/calvin_agent/evaluation/evaluate_policy.py +++ b/calvin_models/calvin_agent/evaluation/evaluate_policy.py @@ -42,7 +42,7 @@ NUM_SEQUENCES = 1000 def get_epoch(checkpoint): if "=" not in checkpoint.stem: return "0" - checkpoint.stem.split("=")[1] + return checkpoint.stem.split("=")[1] def make_env(dataset_path): -- 2.39.5 (Apple Git-154) ```
